name: formal_logic
doc:
FORMAL LOGIC - the laws of Boolean algebra, the inference forms, and NAND/NOR completeness (issue #12,
2026-10-16: a logic floor, down the domain list). Every law here is SEALED BY ITS TRUTH-TABLE PROOF through
formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY, never asserted: the Boolean-algebra laws as equivalences over p, q, r, each in both
dual forms; the inference forms as entailments - four valid, and the two classic fallacies sealed as NOT
entailing (claimed_entailment false: the seal records the fallacy honestly); functional completeness - NOT, AND
and OR each rebuilt from NAND alone and from NOR alone; and one minimization sealed through the minimal_form check
(Quine-McCluskey, exact to four variables). Boole's and Sheffer's postulates are CITED; the theorems are SEALED
(the Euclid rule). Idempotent.

sticks.question: Formal logic - Boolean algebra, inference forms, NAND and NOR
sticks.statement: Every law of propositional logic is a theorem of the two-element Boolean algebra, decided by its truth table.
references: G. Boole, The Laws of Thought (1854)
H. M. Sheffer, A set of five independent postulates for Boolean algebras (1913)

marks.claim: [identity, SEALED] p & True = p: True is the identity for AND (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY). The algebra's two elements, 1 and 0, are the units of its two operations.

[identity, the dual] p | False = p: False is the identity for OR (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY). Every law below has a dual - swap AND with OR and True with False - and the dual is a theorem too.
[domination, SEALED] p & False = False (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): False annihilates under AND.
[domination, the dual] p | True = True (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): True annihilates under OR.
[idempotent, SEALED] p & p = p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): saying it twice adds nothing - unlike arithmetic, where x * x is not x.
[idempotent, the dual] p | p = p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY).
[complement, SEALED] p & ~p = False (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): the law of non-contradiction - a thing and its denial are never both true.
[complement, the dual] p | ~p = True (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): the law of excluded middle - one of them is.
[double negation, SEALED] ~~p = p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): in the two-element algebra a denial denied is the thing itself.
[commutative, SEALED] p & q = q & p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY).
[commutative, the dual] p | q = q | p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY).
[associative, SEALED] (p & q) & r = p & (q & r) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): the grouping does not matter, so a chain of ANDs needs no parentheses.
[associative, the dual] (p | q) | r = p | (q | r) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY).
[distributive, SEALED] p & (q | r) = (p & q) | (p & r) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): AND distributes over OR, as multiplication over addition.

[distributive, the dual] p | (q & r) = (p | q) & (p | r) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): OR distributes over AND too - the law arithmetic does NOT have (a + bc is not (a+b)(a+c)). This is where Boolean algebra parts from the algebra of numbers.
[absorption, SEALED] p & (p | q) = p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): the second factor is swallowed by the first.
[absorption, the dual] p | (p & q) = p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY).

[De Morgan, SEALED] ~(p & q) = ~p | ~q (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): the denial of a conjunction is the disjunction of the denials - 'not both' is 'at least one is not'.
[De Morgan, the dual] ~(p | q) = ~p & ~q (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): 'neither' is 'not this and not that'.
[modus ponens, SEALED] p, p >> q |= q (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY: no row makes both premises true and the conclusion false). The form every deduction stands on.
[modus tollens, SEALED] p >> q, ~q |= ~p (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): deny the consequent and the antecedent falls - the shape of refutation.
[hypothetical syllogism, SEALED] p >> q, q >> r |= p >> r (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): implications chain, which is why a proof can be long.
[disjunctive syllogism, SEALED] p | q, ~p |= q (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): eliminate one branch and the other remains - narrowing by elimination.

[affirming the consequent, SEALED AS A FALLACY] p >> q, q does NOT entail p: the seal records claimed_entailment = false, confirmed by the row p = False, q = True where both premises hold and the conclusion fails. 'If it rained the ground is wet; the ground is wet' does not give rain.

[denying the antecedent, SEALED AS A FALLACY] p >> q, ~p does NOT entail ~q: sealed with claimed_entailment = false, the counter-row p = False, q = True. The engine seals what the table shows - a fallacy is kept as a fallacy, never dressed as a rule.

[NAND is complete: NOT, SEALED] ~p = ~(p & p) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): NOT from a single NAND with both inputs tied together - the first step of Sheffer's stroke.
[NAND is complete: AND, SEALED] p & q = ~(~(p & q) & ~(p & q)) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): AND is a NAND followed by a NAND-as-NOT - two gates.

[NAND is complete: OR, SEALED] p | q = ~(~(p & p) & ~(q & q)) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): OR is De Morgan read through NAND - three gates. With NOT, AND and OR all rebuilt, every Boolean function is reachable from NAND alone: the one gate a whole computer can be wired from.
[NOR is complete: NOT, SEALED] ~p = ~(p | p) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY): the dual stroke (Peirce's arrow).
[NOR is complete: OR, SEALED] p | q = ~(~(p | q) | ~(p | q)) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY).

[NOR is complete: AND, SEALED] p & q = ~(~(p | p) | ~(q | q)) (sealed by its truth table through formal_logic.LOGIC_VERIFY). NOR alone is also complete - the Apollo guidance computer was built from one three-input NOR gate, repeated.

[minimal form, SEALED] (p & q) | (p & ~q) minimizes to p - one product term, and no equivalent sum-of-products has fewer (sealed through formal_logic.minimal_form: Quine-McCluskey prime implicants and an exhaustive minimum cover, exact to four variables). Absorption, read as a circuit: two gates become a wire.

[the postulates, CITED] Boole gave logic an algebra - the laws of thought as equations over 0 and 1 (1854); Sheffer showed the whole algebra rests on five independent postulates and that a single operation, the stroke (NAND), suffices to define the rest (1913). The postulate sets are CITED, never sealed: an axiom is chosen, not proven. Every law above is a THEOREM of those postulates, and each one is sealed by the only proof the two-element algebra needs - its truth table.
marks.source: G. Boole, The Laws of Thought (1854); H. M. Sheffer, A set of five independent postulates for Boolean algebras, Trans. AMS 14 (1913) 481-488

marks.claim: [the bound, stated] Every seal here is an exhaustive truth table over at most three variables - eight rows, complete and exact. The minimal_form check decides minimality exactly to FOUR variables (16 minterms, at most 13 prime implicants, an exhaustive cover); at five or more it returns NOT_APPLICABLE with the reason - bounded, never a guess. First-order logic (quantifiers) is not exposed by the verifier and is declined: a miss stays a miss.

[on the one map] Boolean algebra is one algebra with three faces: logic (this stick), circuits (computer_science.logic_gate - the 16 functions of two inputs) and sets (mathematics.set_algebra - union, intersection, complement obey the same laws). One Boolean core backs all three verifiers. Ties the computer-science stick and card_floor_computer_science.
